newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rand report proposes dedicated Dutch cargo airport.
newsitem.headline: Rand report proposes dedicated Dutch cargo airport.

text.p: A second national airport dedicated to airfreight is proposed in a report commisioned by the Dutch government and drawn up by consultants Rand Europe, although it said there are a number of drawbacks.
It added that a separate cargo airport in the Netherlands would cost less than building a second national airport and would reduce noise at the existing national airport, Amsterdam-Schiphol.

The consultants advised the Dutch ministries of economic affairs, transport and environment that any new Dutch all-cargo airport would also require changes in how air cargo is transported to make it successful.

The industry's reliance on belly space in passenger aircraft would be one of the big barriers, Rand said, while adding that: "Other changes (to make the airport an economic success) would also be largely beyond the control of the Dutch government."
The three ministries commissioned the report as part of a fact finding exercise examining second airport options.
Later this year, the Dutch cabinet will decide how air traffic will be permitted to grow in Holland in the year 2000 and beyond.

The report is designed to inform ministers about growth options. The consultants said locating an airport -- for passengers and airfreight -- offshore would be the most environmentally friendly option, restricted only by the high cost of building a high speed people and cargo transport system.
Expanding Schiphol is, the report said, the cheapest option, but carries with it problems of noise, third party risk and airport traffic related congestion.

The report also looked at locating an airport on the border with Belgium, which Rand said would be best in terms of competitive and geographic position, but warned that such a new piece of infrastructure would be "costly and environmentally damaging." --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
